VHistory - History Info.vi

Owning Palette: Variabe History VIs

Returns information on a variable history. The specified variable must exist; otherwise, the VI returns an error. The VI does not return an error if the specified variable has no history attached. The VHistory - History Controller.vi is used to configure VarMan to maintain the history of a variable.
See Variable History and VarMan overview topics for more information.

Click the parameters for more information

 

VC Handle specifies the handle of the Variable Context in which the target variable exists. To operate on a global variable, pass -1 to this input or keep it unwired. VC Handle is ignored if name_spec refers to the variable by an alias. See the Referring to variables topic for more information.
name_spec defines the name specifier of the target variable. Usually, this is merely a variable name; however, additional options are available. See the Referring to variables topic for details.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
dup name_spec is a flow-through parameter with the same value as name_spec.
history info is a cluster with information on configuration and state of the variable history.
var type indicates the data type code of the specified variable.
history length indicates the maximum number of variable values that can be stored in the history.
stored values indicates the actual number of variable values stored in the history. This value cannot exceed the history length.
update cnt is an incremental counter that contains the total number of values written to the history since it was created. Every time VarMan adds a value to the history, it increments update cnt counter. This value can exceed the history length.
last update ms indicates the Millisecond Timer value (the output of the Tick Count (ms) primitive) when the most recent value was saved to the history.
newest timestamp indicates the time stamp, in seconds, of the most recent value in the history.
oldest timestamp indicates the time stamp, in seconds, of the oldest value stored in the history.
NewVals mode is a cluster with parameters specific for reading a history in the NewVals mode.
NewVals cnt is an incremental counter that contains the number of values saved to the history since it was last read in the NewVals mode. VarMan increments the counter every time it adds a value to the history and zeroes the counter when the history is read in NewVals mode. This value can exceed the history length.
last read time contains time stamp, in seconds, of the last value that has been read in NewVals mode. In fact, VarMan sets this parameter to the current value of the newest timestamp when the history is read in NewVals mode.
last read ms contains time stamp, in millisecond timer's values, of the last value that has been read in NewVals mode. In fact, VarMan sets this parameter to the current value of last update ms when the history is read in NewVals mode.
time condition contains parameters of time conditions used for maintaining the history. See Updating history, Time condition topic for details.
Step, ms indicates a time step, in milliseconds, to update the history.
Gate, ms indicates a time gate, in milliseconds, to overwrite the last value in the history.
value condition contains parameters of value condition used for maintaining the history. See Updating history, Value conditions topic for details on how it works.
condition indicates the kind of condition:

0don't test
1changed
2abs deviation
3rel deviation
4out of range
5within range
Delta indicates the Delta parameter of the value condition.
Range_Min indicates the Range_Min parameter of the value condition.
Range_Max indicates the Range_Max parameter of the value condition.
valid history is TRUE if the specified variable has a history attached. Otherwise, valid history is FALSE; herewith error out does not indicate an error.
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains VarMan VI error code identifying an error if any occurred. If no error occurred, it is equal to zero.
source contains the error description and VI location information if an error occurred.
more data contains additional information about the history.
store Writer IDs indicates whether the history maintains Writer IDs.
